name: The DIY Stopwatch
why_it_works: People choose DIY because it feels free, but they never price their own hours. A running clock makes the hidden cost visible: viewers watch time leak away on one side and finish fast on the other, and they do the math themselves without being lectured.

hook.pattern: Put two clocks on screen and start them at the same moment: a race the viewer has to watch to the end.
examples: Same {{task}}, two clocks. Who finishes first?
DIY {{task}} looks free. Watch what it costs.
I timed a DIY {{task}} against a pro.

variables.name: task
variables.description: The job people try to do themselves

variables.name: diy_time
variables.description: Typical honest time for a first-timer

variables.name: disclosure
variables.description: Required fine-print line for the client's regulated niche, shown small on screen
variables.example: Attorney advertising. Past results do not guarantee a similar outcome.

visual.prompt: Vertical 9:16 split screen, top half a cluttered home garage or desk at night, bottom half a clean professional {{brand}} workspace, a large blank stopwatch shape on each half with the running times added as overlay in the edit, high contrast

beats.voiceover: The DIY way: tutorials, guesswork, starting over.

visual.prompt: Vertical handheld shot of frustrated hands doing the {{task}} at home, phone propped up playing a tutorial, scattered tools, dim overhead bulb, small realistic struggle, no faces
Vertical photo of a professional from {{brand}} finishing the {{task}} with the right tools, bright even shop light, calm focused posture, clean organized background
Vertical photo of a relaxed customer picking up keys or a finished deliverable at the {{brand}} front desk, warm friendly light, {{brand}} logo visible on the wall

craft.notes: Keep both timers visible in every beat as on-screen overlays so the viewer always knows the score. Let the DIY side be relatable, not stupid: the viewer should see themselves in it and laugh, not feel mocked.

do_not: Exaggerate the DIY time; use what a real first-timer would honestly spend
Make the DIY person look dumb; that insults the exact viewer you want to book
Show unsafe DIY work as if it were normal
compliance: Law firms: do not imply DIY legal work always fails or that hiring the firm guarantees an outcome; include the attorney advertising label your state bar requires
Law firms: no client results or time claims unless they are typical and documented
Every time shown must be an honest, typical figure the business can back up
